items.title: A Bad Understander Beats AI At Teaching
items.summary: In episode 1025 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Luis Serrano, Founder of Serrano Academy about the one thing a human teacher has that a model does not. Luis calls himself a better 'bad understander' than any model: he knows exactly where a student gets lost, because he has been lost there himself. Models overlook that, he argues, precisely because they already know everything.

items.title: Does Hexagonal Architecture Work with CQRS and DDD?
items.summary:
Do CQRS, Domain-Driven Design, and Clean Architecture fit together—or just add more layers?

Enrique Medina Montenegro, author of Clean Applications with Hexagonal Architecture, explains how the book uses these ideas together to build a clean, independent application core without unnecessary complexity.

items.title: Topological Intelligence: AI Planning w/ Persistent Homology
items.summary:
In conventional hierarchical goal-conditioned RL, a high-level controller proposes a subgoal, and a low-level policy attempts to reach it.

The subgoal is usually derived from:
- a learned value function;
- a latent action;
- temporal distance;
- visitation frequency;
- graph centrality;
- the representation learned by a particular policy.

These quantities answer questions such as:
Where does this controller prefer to go?
or:
Which state appears useful under this controller’s dynamics?

This new pre-print  asks a more demanding question:
Which region must every successful controller cross?

In short: 
Topology identifies separation and loops. 
Geometry identifies which separating regions are unusually narrow. 
The offline dataset determines which part of the world is even visible to the method.

Now: What if you could rigorously decouple and abstract away a strategic objective from the kinematic relevance of its (robotic) executor using algebraic topology? 

In this video, we explore a new idea that projects raw offline RL trajectories onto a transport-weighted Riemannian manifold to construct a discrete Eikonal triplet, thereby enforcing 1-Lipschitz progress monotonicity along a shortest-path tree. 

New research pre-prints (see also below) show how the authors compute the Hausdorff measure of radial level-sets and apply sublevel-set filtration to extract H0​ persistent homology certificates.

A simple explanation how multiscale H1 persistence generates invariant winding-number signatures to resolve non-contractible trajectory routing for topological memory will be indicated. 

But remember: Homology is kind of an abelian summary. It detects independent loops but does not preserve every distinction between path homotopy classes.

The system observes only successful behavior. A persistent hole can represent:
1. a physical obstacle;
2. an unexplored region;
3. a behavior-policy bias;
4. missing demonstrations;
5. a sensor blind spot.

A more general theory may require:
a.  relative homology for open start-to-goal paths;
b. the fundamental group or groupoid;
c. persistent cohomology;
d. directed topology for irreversible dynamics.
A future system needs active exploration or counterfactual reachability tests to distinguish:
not observed (is different from)  not reachable.

Route topology is most valuable when alternatives matter. The largest Humanoid gain occurs on the multi-route task:
94.8%  versus 58.8%
against the direct map-based reference, a +36.0-point difference.

All rights w/ authors: 
TOPOLOGICAL NECESSITIES: MECHANISM-INVARIANT STRATEGIC SUBGOALS FOR CROSS-EMBODIMENT GOAL-CONDITIONED CONTROL

Xi Li1

items.title: Managed Agents - Don't Get Locked In
items.summary:
In this video, I look at the concept of managed agents that a lot of providers are currently rolling out. While they have a lot of advantages, you also want to ask yourself: do you really want to get locked in for these? 

Twitter: https://x.com/Sam_Witteveen 

🕵️ Interested in building LLM Agents? Fill out the form below
Building LLM Agents Form: https://drp.li/dIMes

04:13 Claude Managed Agents Concepts
05:28 The Economics Behind
08:35 Five Questions to Ask Before Choosing Which One to Choose

items.title: How DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Actually Works: A Deep Dive
items.summary:
Sign up for updates on our NEW AI engineering book: https://www.louisbouchard.ai/book/?utm_source=yt-lf&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=book

Deepseek-V4.1-Flash tech report: https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/main/DeepSeek_V41_Tech_Report.pdf?fbclid=IwY2xjawUPu9VwZG9mA2V4dG4DYWVtAjExAHNydGMGYXBwX2lkATAAAR5ZIQ8DYGcBBTCpNihWDOEibcCkNerVHRv5HPbtV56YflMjzP1LS4p9Wxfe7w_aem_rfnVBAxmIPNX12ZEIy2WRQ

Our Context Engineering workshop at @aiDotEngineer : https://youtu.be/WP3hjUXd918

►https://www.louisbouchard.ai/learnai/

Become a member of the YouTube community, support my work and get a cool Discord role :
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCUzGQrN-lyyc0BWTYoJM_Sg/join

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash review for AI engineers: what changed over V4 Flash, how its causal encoder-decoder architecture and CSA2 reduce KV cache memory, and what our writing benchmark says about cost, quality, and high versus max effort. I walk through the paper’s results and limits before sharing where I’d use this open-weight model.

Writing results shown are from our September 10, 2026 snapshot: 148 configurations, 10 tasks, 5 drafts per configuration per task, and 3 blind model judges. We’ll share more about the benchmark soon.

Cache figures refer to global or persistent KV state as labeled. Writing costs are token-based averages for the tested routes and rates; Claude Code costs use API-equivalent accounting. Results and timing depend on the task and provider.

Chapters:
00:00 - Introduction: DeepSeek Flash V4.1
02:04 - Why KV Cache Matters for Agent Costs
03:23 - DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Overview & Specs
04:50 - Optimization 1: Split Architecture & Causal Encoder
06:04 - Optimization 2: Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA2)
07:53 - Optimization 3: Deployment & Cache Replay
09:25 - Performance, Benchmarks & Agentic Tasks
10:31 - The Reasoning Effort Dial
10:56 - Writing Benchmark Results
13:11 - Final Takeaways & Upcoming Book Announcement

items.title: You Can Photocopy an AI's Weights. That's the Problem.
items.summary:
Edward Hughes explains why open weights remove a constraint that once helped produce human creativity — and why the emerging job is constraint engineering.

Watch the full conversation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P4bYjTJvD28
